chapter: Follow-up questions, Bird and the Ellington sidemen
title: Hank Jones's playing and their planned two-piano duo
summary: Jones says Hank Jones sounds like him; they rehearsed a two-piano duo at Steinway Hall that nobody would book.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Who played piano: the pianists musicians remembered

blocks.x: You mentioned something on an earlier tape that you said that Hank Jones could play things that you can't play, or you can write things for Hank Jones that you couldn't play.
Yeah.
Things like what? I mean, really?
Oh, well --
Or was that just a way of complimenting Hank Jones?
Okay. Well, half and half, because there
I kind of thought so. I know Hank Jones is a fine piano player.

But I'll say one thing. There was one thing that Hank did on a record date with Joe Williams, and I voiced the chords my way, and Hank and I have a similar touch, and I listened to Hank, I said, 'Gee whiz, it sounds like me.'
(Laughter)
I thought it was me for a minute, you know. And we sounded quite a bit alike. In fact we had a duet at one time.
You and Hank?
Yeah.
Oh, I know he's doing that with John Lewis now.
Yeah, well we had --
When was that?
Oh, this goes back some time ago. We used to go to Steinway Hall and rent a piano, rent two great big Baldwins, and rehearse just as religiously.
Oh.
But we couldn't sell it. We couldn't get anybody to be interested in it, you know?
About how long ago was that?
Oh, let me see. I think it's about in
the '50s, late '50s.
Uh-huh. That would be nice to hear.
Yeah. Oh, we had a ball, you know?
